risks.title: Short Default Cure and Eviction Notice
risks.original_clause:
Section 6. Termination and Default
In the event of non-payment of rent or material violation of lease covenants that remains uncured for fourteen (14) days after written notice, Landlord may terminate this lease and commence eviction proceedings under applicable state law.
risks.explanation: A 14-day cure window applies before the landlord may initiate formal eviction proceedings following an alleged default.
risks.why_it_matters: A narrow 14-day timeline may provide limited opportunity to resolve disputed rent charges or address maintenance issues.
risks.possible_consequences: Risk of expedited legal eviction proceedings and lease forfeiture.
suggested_questions: Can the default cure window be expanded to a standard 30-day period?
Can written notice via registered mail be required prior to legal action?
risks.evidence_quote:

risks.title: Security Deposit Forfeiture Terms
risks.original_clause:
Section 3. Security Deposit
Upon execution of this Agreement, Tenant shall deposit with Landlord the sum of ,400.00 as a security deposit. The security deposit will be returned within thirty (30) days after vacating, less any deductions for unpaid rent or repairs for physical damage beyond normal wear and tear.
risks.explanation: The agreement grants the landlord broad rights to deduct repair expenses, unpaid rent, and restoration costs from the deposit.
risks.why_it_matters: Tenants could experience substantial deductions without itemized repair invoices or move-in condition documentation.
risks.possible_consequences: Partial or full loss of the deposit amount upon lease termination.
suggested_questions: Can a requirement for itemized repair receipts within 30 days of move-out be added?
Can joint move-in and move-out inspection walk-throughs be formally stipulated?
risks.evidence_quote:

risks.title: Subletting and Assignment Prohibition
risks.original_clause:
Section 4. Use of Premises and Assignment
The Premises shall be used solely as a private residential dwelling. Tenant shall not assign this lease, sublet the premises, or grant any license to use the premises without the express prior written consent of Landlord.
risks.explanation: The agreement prohibits assigning, subletting, or transferring occupancy rights without prior written consent from the landlord.
risks.why_it_matters: Tenants cannot transfer lease obligations or sublease to roommates if personal circumstances require relocation.
risks.possible_consequences: Potential risk of default or eviction if unauthorized occupants reside on the premises.
suggested_questions: Can subletting be permitted subject to reasonable landlord screening and consent?
Can a mutual lease reassignment fee be defined to avoid forfeiture?
